messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Service alert: P95 latency on /v1/generate exceeded 1.2s for the past 3m, queue depth on batcher-prod > 1200. Possible batching regression. Paging oncall.
Aisha: Oncall here. I'm looking. Any recent deploys to runtime or batcher?
Mark: Not a user-facing deploy in last hour. Rolling kernel tweak in infra yesterday but nothing touching batch config. Pulling metrics now.
Sam: I'm seeing increased average batch assembly time in batcher-prod, tail waits up ~3x. Could be continuous-batching parameters being too aggressive for current traffic spike.
Aisha: Customer impact? Which tiers / routes?
Sam: Mostly free and dev-tier traffic hitting /v1/generate-admin (no auth) and a spike from a noisy customer in eu-west. Premium routes slightly affected but still under 800ms P95.
Priya: I'm seeing 5 distinct IPs pushing large prompt sizes, causing big KV cache churn. Might be contributing.
Aisha: Ok live mitigation plan: 1) tighten continuous batching window (trade a little latency for throughput predictability) 2) apply emergency rate limit to free tier 3) disable model-variant fallback that does expensive function-calls for anonymous routes 4) monitor.
Mark: Agreed. I'll change max_batch_delay from 40ms -> 12ms and clamp max_batch_size 1024 -> 512 for batcher-prod.
Aisha: Mark please post the exact commands so I can annotate incident timeline.
Mark: Running now.
```
# reduce batching delay and max size
redwoodctl set batcher batcher-prod --max_delay=12ms --max_batch_size=512
```
Mark: Command applied. deploy-bot: config-update event id=cfg_202603151230
deploy-bot: :gear: batcher-prod config updated by Mark (runtime team)
Sam: I'm putting a soft quota on free tier routes to 60 req/min per IP to curb noisy inputs.
```
# emergency quota via admin API
curl -X POST https://internal.console.redwood.ai/admin/quotas
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY'
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","tier":"free","quota_per_min":60}'
```
Priya: Quota applied. incident-bot: quota-change event id=q_188123
Aisha: Also disable the expensive function-call model variant for anonymous routes.
Mark: patching routing table now.
```
redwoodctl set route /v1/generate --disable-variant model-fncall-v2 --pool=batcher-prod
```
Mark: Done.
Sam: Initial telemetry after changes: queue depth dropped from 1200 -> 300 in ~60s, p95 overall down 1.2s -> 650ms, tail latency still a bit noisy for large prompts.
Aisha: Good. Priya can you contact the known noisy customer in eu-west to ask them to throttle? Put them on temporary stricter quota.
Priya: Reached out via support ticket and applied IP-level throttle for their IP block.
Aisha: We're going to hold these mitigations for 20m and re-evaluate. If stable, we'll roll a more measured config: maybe 20ms batch delay and dynamic per-route batching profiles.
Sam: Agree. I'll spin up a canary with adaptive batching off and route traffic to it for further tests.
Mark: Note: this tradeoff increases median latency slightly for small requests, but reduces tail and keeps throughput up. Documenting in incident log.
Aisha: Handing off monitoring to Priya for the next 30m. I'll stay available for escalation.
Priya: Monitoring dashboard looks good. No new alerts in last 5m. :white_check_mark:
Aisha: Thanks team. Will update postmortem with root cause suspects: sudden noisy traffic + aggressive continuous-batching defaults + function-call heavy variant.
Sam: Suggest follow-ups: add auto-throttle for anomalous IPs, per-route batching profiles, and a feature-flag to disable expensive variants per route without full routing change.
Mark: I'll open infra tasks for instrumentation and an AB test to find optimal max_delay per pool.
Aisha: Closing this thread for now, keeping incident open in tracker. If anything changes ping me. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-15-1881234567 created, severity P2, status mitigated (live mitigations applied).
